newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU committee meets on Italy EMU convergence plans.
newsitem.headline: EU committee meets on Italy EMU convergence plans.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee met on Wednesday to review Italy's renewed efforts to consolidate its public finances ahead of economic and monetary union.
"We hope to have Italy's convergence programme," said one source familiar with the committee's agenda.
On Tuesday the Italian Senate -- the upper house of parliament -- approved the centre-left government's three-year programme of key economic targets.
The financial plan sets out strict targets for 1998-2000 to keep Italy on course to join Europe's planned single currency.

EU monetary affairs commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy on Tuesday welcomed Italy's economic programme but warned that the country's "moment of truth" regarding qualification for the euro would come in September when it is expected to adopt budgetary measures for 1998.
He added that the plan itself was not a guarantee that Italy would be in the first wave of countries creating a single currency.
Monetary sources said the regularly scheduled meeting would also focus on drawing up legislation for the future European Central Bank.
In particular, the group will attempt to define the legal basis for the bank's minimum reserves policy, or the method by which monetary control is implemented.
There is also a need to agree on the statistical data that will be used to define the weightings of the share each national central bank will have in the ECB's capital.
The European System of Central Banks will be composed of the ECB and national central banks participating in the euro.
